card.title: Our Private Language
card.instruction: Use old references, shorthand, and familiar rhythms as proof that this connection exists beneath whatever has changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two taps: rescue me from this reunion speech. You remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the headteacher now. I wrote it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm still the person you signalled when assembly ran long.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cut a paragraph. Keep your glass still; you're distracting me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One glass down, one paragraph gone. We still get each other out of assembly.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 uses an old rescue rhythm, A3 invokes shared assembly escapes despite B's new title, and A5 recognizes the edited speech as the same partnership.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's authorship and headteacher role prompt A3's shared past; B4's paragraph cut and quiet-glass request become A5's reciprocal signal.

relationship.evidence: B2 has responsibility for the speech and B4 compromises while asking A to stop distracting the delivery.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's cut paragraph and lowered glass to make a current two-person version of their old escape.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a reunion speech, and B2-A3 explain the changed and former school roles.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's one-glass-one-paragraph rhythm echoes the practical exchange B4 proposed.
